newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cambodian first premier says Hun Sen seeks coup.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian first premier says Hun Sen seeks coup.

text.p: Cambodian First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh on Saturday accused his rival, second Prime Minister Hun Sen, of trying to stage a coup against him in order to derail democratic elections set for May 1998.
"We consider that what is currently happening in Phnom Penh is a coup d'etat perpetuated by Mr Hun Sen," a statement attributed to Ranariddh said.
The statement was faxed to news agencies in Paris, where Ranariddh was said to be visiting family. A spokesman for the first prime minister could not immediately be reached to verify the fax.
Fighting broke out in Phnom Penh on Saturday between groups of soldiers loyal to Hun Sen and others loyal to Ranariddh after Hun Sen ordered a crackdown on "illegal troops" under Ranariddh's command.

In the statement, Ranariddh said the fighting resulted because "Hun Sen does not want free and democratic elections scheduled for May 1998". He urged the international community not to recognise any regime resulting from the use of force and urged Cambodia's armed forces and royal police not to follow Hun Sen and his supporters "in their illegal and criminal adventure which puts our country in great danger".
